exercises.title: A list with a dummy head
exercises.task: Read List. It starts with a dummy node that holds no value, so removing the first real node is no special case: every removal changes some prev.next. Run removes values from the front, the middle and the end.

exercises.title: Reverse a list
exercises.task: Reverse the list in place by turning each arrow around as you walk. Three pointers: the node before, the current node, and the one after (save it before you change cur.next).
hints: Start with prev = nil and cur = l.head.next (the first real node).
In the loop: save next := cur.next, point cur.next at prev, then move both prev and cur one step.
When the loop ends, prev is the old last node: hang it after the dummy head.

exercises.title: An LRU cache
exercises.task: A cache that keeps the capacity most recently used keys and evicts the least recently used one. Use Go's container/list (a doubly linked list) for the order and a map from key to list element for the O(1) lookup. Hover over list. names in the editor for their documentation.
hints: Keep the most recent at the front: MoveToFront on every Get and Put of an existing key.
The map holds *list.Element; store an entry{key, value} in the element, so that when you evict the back you know which key to delete from the map.
